title: Factors Considered in Drawing up COMPASS Shortage Occupation List
what_it_is: Factors Considered in Drawing up COMPASS Shortage Occupation List

sections.label: Shortage Occupation List criteria
sections.summary: MOM and MTI evaluate occupations for the COMPASS Shortage Occupation List based on three criteria: strategic importance, labour shortage, and sector commitment to local pipeline.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) evaluate occupations for the Complementarity Assessment Framework or COMPASS' Shortage Occupation List (SOL) based on three criteria: the first criterion being the strategic importance of the occupation to Singapore’s economic priorities; second, the degree and nature of labour shortage; and third, the sector’s commitment to developing the local pipeline to address these shortages.

sections.label: Industry commitment to local pipeline
sections.summary: Occupations are included in the SOL only with clear industry plans and commitments to develop the local pipeline, which are reviewed as a condition for renewal.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: While the SOL helps companies access foreign professionals to plug immediate skills gaps and seize economic opportunities, it must also be complemented by robust efforts by industry to train up and place locals into these well-paying jobs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Hence, there must be clear plans, clear commitments by industry to develop the local pipeline, or else the occupation will not be included in the SOL.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Rather than mandating fixed commitments for each firm, sector agencies have the flexibility to work closely with the firms, industry partners and education and training providers on plans to train and employ more locals with these skills in shortage.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: We will review that these commitments are met, as a key condition for renewing an occupation on the SOL.

sections.label: SOL reset and annual adjustment
sections.summary: The SOL will be reset every three years and adjusted annually to add or remove occupations if industry demand or skilled worker supply changes significantly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The SOL will be reset every three years and we intend to adjust it annually to add or remove occupations if there are significant changes in industry demand or supply of skilled workers.

sections.label: Regular SOL review and reset
sections.summary: The SOL will be reviewed regularly and adjusted annually, starting on a fresh slate every three years to avoid entrenching dependencies in any occupation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The SOL, as I have shared earlier on, will be reviewed regularly to reflect current industry needs and shortages; and of course, in addition to earlier on, the adjustments annually.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: This will start on a fresh slate every three years so that we do not entrench any particular dependencies in any occupation.

sections.label: Monitoring wage changes
sections.summary: Wage changes over time are monitored, and qualifying salaries for the Employment Pass and S Pass minimum qualifying salaries are calibrated upwards by age.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: To the Member's second supplementary question about whether we monitor wage changes over time, indeed, we do, and that is why we have also been calibrating upwards our qualifying salary with regard to the Employment Pass as well as our S Pass minimum qualifying salaries.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And that follows a graduated skill depending on the age of the foreign work pass holder.
